In terms of light intensity stability, we exposed unencapsulated devices to a LED solar simulator with adjustable intensity (0.5 sun, 1 sun and 1.2 sun). The devices are tested at open circuit condition in a home build nitrogen box without cooling (~35-40°C). Figure 4 plots the average PCEs (absolute values) of 4 devices aged at each light intensity. Under 0.5 sun condition, the device retains 95% of its initial PCE after 500 hours of illumination. Under 1 sun condition, the device retains 90% of its initial PCE after 400 hours of illumination. Under 1.3 sun condition, the devices retain 85% of its initial PCE after 270 hours of illumination. In summary, the results in Figure 8.4 indicate that there is a negative correlation between different light intensity and device stability (Milestone 1.2.4). Figure 8.4. Page 51 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology Project 9: Lead Sealing Barrier Layers The lead sealing barrier film is based on inexpensive, non-toxic polymers and calcium phosphate, as listed in Figure 9.1(a). The component materials are poly(methyl methacrylate-co- methacrylic acid) (PMMA), poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO), butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) binder, and calcium phosphate salt. The barrier film is designed to convert dissolved Pb2+ into more stable, less soluble forms, preventing Pb from leaching out into the surrounding environment from damaged perovskite solar cells. A cation exchange reaction takes place between Ca2+ from the calcium phosphate in the barrier film and Pb2+ in solution to form less soluble lead phosphate. Photographs of the devices deposited with the barrier film (yellow colored) are shown in Figure 9.1(b). We first assessed whether the barrier film had any impact on the device performance and stability. Figures 9.1(c) and 9.1(d) respectively show the absolute and normalized efficiency of the devices under maximum power point tracking at AM1.5G continuous illumination. The control device (without barrier film) had an initial PCE of ~22%. With the addition of the barrier film, the efficiency dropped to ~21%.
